newsitem.title: USA: COMEX Dec copper ends at five-week closing high.
newsitem.headline: COMEX Dec copper ends at five-week closing high.

text.p: COMEX December copper futures ended at their highest close in five weeks Thursday, though both COMEX December copper and LME three-month copper briefly saw higher levels intraday two weeks ago.

"The U.S. prompt market remains tight, the Sumitomo effect is probably over and there was talk Friday's LME warehouse stocks data may show another large drawdown," E.D. & F. Man trader Fred Demler said.
COMEX December copper ended up 1.90 cents at 92.25 cents a lb after trading in a 90.20 to 92.40 cent range.
COMEX copper stocks fell 584 short tons Wednesday to 18,242 short tons, following a 8,626 tonne drawdown in LME stocks Tuesday to 220,950 tonnes.

The December/March spread firmed to close at 1.25 cents, from 1.00 cent at Wednesday's close, and has widened from a backwardation of 0.50 cent on Sept 20, reflecting the tightness of the prompt market and the stock draws, analysts said.
"There's been a good underlying tone for some weeks and we're coming into what is seasonally a good demand period," Demler said.
"But it's true that longer term demand projections dont match rising supply capacity," he said.
